newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says succeeds in limiting cocoa pest.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says succeeds in limiting cocoa pest.

text.p: An Indonesian cocoa industry official said on Thursday experiments with new pruning techniques had dramatically limited the cocoa pod borer pest in the key growing region of South Sulawesi.

"The results have been fantastic after eight months of trial on demonstration plots," Halim Razak, vice-chairman of the Indonesia Cocoa Association, told Reuters by phone from the main growing region's capital Ujung Pandang.
"We are now holding a three-day workshop for 100 farmers to explain to them the techniques we used in the demonstration plots," Razak said. The workshop ends on Friday.
Razak said crop loss due to the pest on the five one-hectare plots was a mere five percent compared with 30 to 35 percent in other areas infested with the pod borer.
"This means crop yield in areas affected with the pod borer can increase by about 30 percent if farmers use the same techniques applied on the demonstration plots," he said.

The techniques were introduced by British entomologist John Mumford of London University's Imperial College and involve regular pruning of the cocoa tree, and regular, frequent and complete harvesting of cocoa pods.
